name: keeperOverrun
title: A replicated commit outlives the lease margin (SLACK 2 > MARGIN 1) and lands after another worker took the lane and inserted the batch
timing: model time is in ticks; a worker's fence = sent + TTL - MARGIN - BUDGET, its statement lands by fence + BUDGET + SLACK, another worker may take the lane at sent + TTL + MARGIN (MARGIN = BUDGET = 1 tick)

steps.action: PUT e1/000 with request 1; S3 commits it
check (absent) and send INSERT S1 over e1/0 with fence 1

changes.statements in flight: S1 fence 1; lands by fence + BUDGET + SLACK = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4

steps.action: S1 passes its fence, writes its part, and its Keeper commit request hangs (a frozen or partitioned Keeper node); the server retries up to the session timeout
four ticks: w1 is silent (paused, or waiting on S1)
takeover at the earliest: it has seen lease version (sent 0) for TTL + MARGIN = 4
count check: e1/0 absent (S1 not landed); send INSERT S2
FATAL: S1's commit lands at t=4 <= 4, past its fence (Keeper answered the retry loop)

design.guard: SLACK <= MARGIN: a statement lands by fence + BUDGET + SLACK = sent + TTL + SLACK - MARGIN, strictly before the earliest takeover at sent + TTL + MARGIN
design.effect: with SLACK 1, S1 lands by 3 < 4; at the takeover cApply(S1) is disabled (keeperOverrunDesignTest), so w2's check sees whatever S1 wrote
design.code: D9/D13: the worker refuses to start with a margin below --keeper-slack (20 s; the replicas' Keeper session timeout minus the budget); measured: a commit 19.0 s past a 10 s max_execution_time

dropped: the writer's 200 and ack; the edge's three steps merged into step 1; step 4 is narrative only (the model's statement simply stays in flight)
